newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends above 6,300 for first time.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends above 6,300 for first time.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average closed above 6,300 points for the first time Thursday as the latest good news on the inflation front energised the blue-chip index to its seventh consecutive record finish.
The Dow ended up 38.76 points at 6,313.00, beating Wednesday's milestone of 6,274.24 and matching the unbroken string of seven highs set in February.
The Nasdaq Composite index also set a new high, gaining 9.64 to 1,270.36. The NYSE Composite rose 2.10 to 389.01, a record.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,464 to 970 on active volume of 478 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"We are seeing a significant capitulation of the bearish camp," said Eugene Peroni, chief technical analyst with Janney, Montgomery Scott. "There is a wider gap between the bulls and the bears and a greater urgency to participate as we cross the next century mark."
The market enjoyed more good economic news, which reinforced the view that the economy is slowing from its brisk pace and inflation is still under control.

The Consumer Price Index rose a moderate 0.3 percent in October after being up an identical amount in September. The data on inflation came one day after the Federal Reserve held interest rates unchanged.
Wall Street welcomed news that retail sales rose just 0.2 percent in October, which was slightly below Wall Street's forecast of a 0.3 percent rise.

"We got some excellent economic news on CPI and retail sales for the bond market, confirming slow growth and benign inflation and the equity market took its cue from the bond market," said Philip Orlando of Value Line Asset Management.

On Wednesday, the government said the Producer Price Index last month rose 0.4 percent, but the core rate, excluding the volatile food and energy components, fell 0.3 percent -- the sharpest drop since the 0.4 percent decline in October 1994.

In the inflation-sensitive bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 13/32, or $4.0625 per $1,000 face value, lowering its yield to a new eight-month low of 6.42 percent from 6.45 percent on Wednesday.
The Dow's string of records matched the seven set from Feb. 5 to 13 this year. It has risen nearly 300 points over the past nine sessions.

Describing the recent powerful run in stocks, Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp., said it is "surprising. Borderline euphoria. You look at the tech sector and it's eye-popping. After that you have to start using Marvel comic book words like 'Shazam!'"
Johnson said investors were scooping up blue-chip stocks and "some defensive sectors, including consumer non-cyclicals and financials showing the best performance aside from technology."

"Interest rates are low and inflation is very much in check," said Janney, Montgomery Scott's Peroni. "There is little bad news out there. Right now, there's so much liquidity it's bulldozing concerns about corporate earnings growth for 1997. It's a frenetic pace."
Among interest-rate sensitive stocks, Merrill Lynch rose one to 78-7/8 after hitting a 52-week high of 80 and Citicorp added 2-1/8 to 104-1/8.
In the technology sector, International Business Machines rose 2-1/4 to 136-7/8 and Microsoft surged 4-5/8 to 149-5/8.
Nokia jumped 7-1/2 to 58-1/2 in U.S. trading after the Finnish telecommunications firm reported lower results for the first nine months but a 58 percent jump in mobile phone sales.
In sympathy, Sweden's Telefom AB L.M. Ericsson added 1-7/8 to 31-1/2 and Motorola rose 2-3/4 to 54-5/8.
Digital Equipment was up two to 33-1/4 after saying it expects its 1997 earnings to top analysts' expectations.
Tiffany lost 2-1/2 to 35-5/8 despite reporting strong third-quarter earnings. Analysts said investors were spooked about the Christmas shopping season for all retailers.

Among other retailers, Federated Department Stores fell 1-3/4 to 32-7/8 and TJX Cos. lost 3/4 to 41-3/4. Sears was off 1-3/8 to 48-1/2, J.C. Penney was off 5/8 to 50-1/4 and Gap slipped 1/2 to 31-3/8.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 4.75 points to 735.88. The American Stock Exchange index was up 1.05 to 585.36.
The average NYSE share was up 22 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 7,121.194 up 38.091 or 0.54 percent.
